Hi Sofia — attaching our Q2 rate card for Hosted API (see attachment). Quick answers while Rishi composes the engineering-backed write-up: 

- System messages: counted as input tokens. Anything you pass in (system + user + tool input) is input.
- Tool calls / function-style integrations: the prompt portion (function signature + args) that is included in the model context is input. The textual output produced by model/tool and returned to the user is billed as output tokens.
- Rounding: we do not do per-call 100-token rounding. Tokens are tracked precisely; invoices compute token totals over the billing period. For small customers we sometimes explain costs conservatively to account for variance.

Sofia — thanks, good questions. Below is the canonical accounting we use for Hosted API invoicing and a few concrete examples you can drop into procurement docs.

Summary rules (short):
- Everything serialized into the model context (system messages, user messages, tool invocation syntax/args that the model sees) counts as input tokens.
- Model-generated text returned by the assistant (including structured JSON returned by a function/tool) counts as output tokens.
- Tokens consumed internally by the runtime for padding/batching are not charged to customers; we only bill the tokenized content that the model actually processes as context or produces as output.
- Streaming vs non-streaming: same accounting. Streaming simply breaks output into chunks for transmission; all generated tokens are charged as output.
- Rounding: we measure tokens as integer tokens (tokenizer output). There is no per-request upward rounding policy; we aggregate token counts per-account across the billing period and multiply by the per-token rates. Invoice line items round dollar amounts to the cent but token counts are exact integers.

Concrete examples (token counts are illustrative):
1) Simple chat turn
   - system: 12 tokens
   - user prompt: 48 tokens
   - model generates: 220 tokens
   => billed input = 60 tokens, billed output = 220 tokens.

2) Tool/function call where model requests retrieval and the retrieval text is inserted back into the context:
   - system: 10 tokens
   - user: 30 tokens
   - function call metadata (signature + serialized args) included in context: 18 tokens
   - retrieval text returned by the external tool and then presented to the model (i.e., tool output inserted into the conversation): 140 tokens
   - model final answer produced after tool use: 200 tokens
   => billed input = 10 + 30 + 18 + 140 = 198 tokens (because when the tool output is inserted for the next model call, it becomes part of the context for that call and is counted as input); billed output = 200 tokens (the assistant's final generated text).

Notes on caching and prefix/KV cache: cached KV entries that are not serialized into the request context are not re-billed. However, if cached content is materialized and sent into the model context for a request (for example, a policy snippet is injected into the prompt), that materialized text is billed as input tokens.

Edge cases:
- If you use automatic prefix injection (e.g., the SDK injects a system prompt on every call), those tokens are billed as input each time unless you use our conversation caching option that pins the prefix on the server side without re-serializing it per-request (ask us about conversation pinning).
- For batched requests we compute tokenization per request and then aggregate; batching does not change what tokens are billed, though batching can reduce compute and therefore cost to Redwood (not passed back as a reduction in token billing).

Invoice/discount mechanics:
- Pricing in the Q2 rate card is per-input-token and per-output-token (distinct rates). Discounts for committed usage are applied at invoice time based on the committed tier. We can provide an estimated monthly cost for the POC at the tier you expect and include a temporary promo if needed.

If you want, I can produce a one-page PDF explanation with the worked examples and include that as part of the SOW.
